summary: Give each replica its own visible log so agreement becomes a comparison between logs rather than a claim.
objective: Build a cluster view where a leader replicates log entries, followers apply them in order and I can partition the network to see what stalls.
intent_signals: Show how replicas agree on an ordered log.
Demonstrate what a network partition does to a replicated cluster.
example_prompts: Build a consensus cluster where I can append entries, partition nodes and watch logs converge.
Show a leader replicating entries and followers applying them in the same order.
negative_signals: Not an implementation of any specific consensus protocol; this is a teaching view with a declared, simplified rule set.
Not a performance, latency or availability model for any real system.
not_for: Not an implementation of any specific consensus protocol; this is a teaching view with a declared, simplified rule set.
Not a performance, latency or availability model for any real system.

entities.name: Replica nodes
entities.guidance: Give every node its own log column, current term or epoch and role badge, so disagreement is visible per node.

entities.name: Message flow
entities.guidance: Show append and acknowledgement messages as objects in flight that can be delayed or dropped, since message loss is the interesting case.

entities.name: Commit marker
entities.guidance: Draw the commit point on each log explicitly, so applied and merely stored entries are visually different.

state_contract.model: A fixed leader and fixed membership with no elections: per-node logs of ordered entries, per-index acknowledgements, in-flight messages with delay, drop and deliver controls, and a commit rule that an entry is committed once a declared majority has acknowledged it. Committed entries are applied in index order. Convergence after healing additionally requires retry of undelivered messages, which is a declared part of this simplified rule set.
state_contract.authority: The per-node logs are authoritative. A node may only apply an entry after the stated commit condition, and the shared state view must be a replay of committed entries rather than a separate object.
actions: Append a client entry at the leader.
Delay, drop or deliver a message.
Partition the cluster and heal it.

invariants: Two nodes never apply different entries at the same log index. Uncommitted suffixes may legitimately differ between nodes, so agreement is asserted over applied entries only.
An entry is applied only after the stated commit condition holds, not when it is merely received.

After healing, logs converge only with the fixed leader, retry and eventual successful delivery of required messages; continued drops may prevent convergence and are reported. Recovery preserves leader index order rather than interleaving divergent suffixes.
motion_guidance: Animate messages travelling with visible latency so ordering and loss are observable events.
Do not fade a node into agreement; agreement must be reached by delivered messages.
known_limits: Fixed leader and membership only; no term changes, election algorithm or log compaction is simulated.
The scene demonstrates behaviour under authored scenarios and proves nothing about a protocol implementation.

Fixed leader and fixed membership: elections, term changes and log compaction are outside this rule set, and adding elections would need safe leadership and log-matching rules that this scene does not model.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Consensus algorithms are used so that servers agree on the commands in their logs, and once a decision is reached it is final; the algorithm must ensure that if one state machine applies a given command as its nth command, no other state machine applies a different nth command.
claims.scope: Safety framing quoted from the cited project page, which concerns commands applied by state machines. This recipe implements a simplified fixed-leader rule set that the page does not analyse, so nothing here is a proof that the simplified rule is safe.

source_refs.locator: Raft project page, consensus and replicated state machines

object_craft.structure: Node bodies carrying a vertical log stack of entry tiles with index labels and a role badge on the front face.
object_craft.material: Neutral node material with one accent reserved for the current leader and a distinct treatment for unreachable nodes.
object_craft.articulation: Entry tiles stack upward as entries are appended; the commit marker slides along the stack.

object_craft.structure: Message capsules travelling along explicit link tubes between nodes, with a visible direction and payload label.
object_craft.material: Capsule materials differ for append and acknowledgement so traffic type is readable at a glance.
object_craft.articulation: Capsules pause when delayed and vanish with a distinct cue when dropped.

physical_contract.scope: Authored message transport along links at chosen speeds; no physical dynamics or collision.
driving: Message speed and delivery are set by the scenario controls, not by forces.
checks: No two nodes apply different entries at the same index; uncommitted suffixes are excluded from the comparison.

With retry enabled and the leader stable, committed prefixes become identical across reachable nodes after healing; with drops still active the scene reports non-convergence rather than forcing agreement.
